title: Someone Buys My Bad DAYS 🧾
premise: At a returns shop in a sunny town you can hand back a bad day before midnight and it never happened, but the fine print says returned days are restocked and sold, and I find that somebody has bought every one of the 47 I returned.
twist: My dad has been buying my returned bad days for four dollars each, because the bad days were the only days I ever called him, and every return took the call away; I keep today and drive him home.
world: A mint-and-cream returns shop with a long counter, a brass bell and a stamp, a dim back room of tall shelves of little gray boxes you can hear, and a small yellow kitchen with an old wall phone.
